title: From the bound to the simplified loss
goal:
Check Equation 12 numerically. With $p_\theta(x_{t-1}|x_t) = \mathcal{N}(\mu_\theta, \sigma_t^2 I)$, the term $L_{t-1}$ of the bound (Equation 5) has the form $\frac{1}{2\sigma_t^2}\|\tilde\mu_t - \mu_\theta\|^2$ plus a constant (Equation 8). With the $\epsilon$ parameterization of Equation 11 it becomes $w_t\,\|\epsilon - \epsilon_\theta\|^2$.

`bound_weight(t, betas, alpha_bars, sigma2)` returns $w_t = \frac{\beta_t^2}{2\sigma_t^2\alpha_t(1-\bar\alpha_t)}$, the weight in Equation 12. `sigma2` is the value of $\sigma_t^2$.

`kl_term_from_eps(eps, eps_pred, t, betas, alpha_bars, sigma2)` returns the KL divergence $D_{KL}(q(x_{t-1}|x_t,x_0) \,\|\, p_\theta(x_{t-1}|x_t))$ for one example when $\sigma_t^2 = \tilde\beta_t$, written as $w_t\|\epsilon - \epsilon_\theta\|^2$. The tests compare it with the KL divergence between two Gaussians, computed directly.
hints: `kl_term_from_eps` is the weight times the squared norm of `eps - eps_pred`, summed over the data dimensions.
Two Gaussians with the same covariance $\sigma^2 I$ have $D_{KL} = \|\mu_1 - \mu_2\|^2 / (2\sigma^2)$. That is how the tests build the reference.
